Subject: Post-call: rapid cutover considerations — hosted vs private VPC

Aaron — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Short recap + concrete asks so we can move fast given the surge you saw this morning that degraded your Hosted throughput.

Summary of what we heard on call:
- Incident: sustained request spike + traffic pattern change causing tail latency and short-term throttling on the Hosted tier.
- Hard constraints: must preserve PII residency in us-west, procurement lead time is tight (procurement@finlytics.com on copy), and the app cannot tolerate >300ms 95th token latency for critical flows.

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Short-term mitigation (Hosted): temporary increased capacity + routing policy tweaks. Fastest but not guaranteed for sustained peak and data residency is limited to our hosted regions. Expected SLA change: no private network isolation.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput, isolated capacity, can be provisioned in the same region; typical lead time ~48–72 hours if we can confirm instance sizes and legal/PO.
3) Private VPC (customer VPC / managed on-prem equivalent): full network isolation and data control, longer lead time (3–7 business days depending on access), requires procurement & infra signoff.

From us — immediate asks for qualification so we can produce a rapid path and quote: please reply with the following by EOD today if possible:
A) Which of the above options is acceptable as an interim (Hosted increase vs Dedicated immediate) vs final (Dedicated vs Private VPC)?
B) Estimated sustained RPS and max burst RPS for the endpoint (critical flows).
C) Data residency / network egress constraints (do you require VPC peering or express route?).
D) Legal/procurement contact and PO timeline (Procurement copied).

Attachments: rapid-cutover-checklist.xlsx (simple checklist we build for capacity cutovers).

If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min runbook call with our Solutions infra team as early as tomorrow morning.

— Hannah
